transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-04 14:30 PST
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jamal Rivers (Redwood SE); Laura Chen (SentraHealth, CTO); Omar Ruiz (SentraHealth, Platform Eng); Priya Shah (SentraHealth, Data Security)

Summary:
Quick sync on last week's production-like run that surfaced intermittent 5xxs and long tail latencies. Root-cause hypotheses narrowed to a combination of a KV-cache eviction pattern + upstream bursty retries causing queue saturation; telemetry gaps made it hard to correlate client retry timing to server-side load. Agreed next steps include a coordinated soak test, log bundle export, and instrumentation additions.

Topics: telemetry gaps, rate limit headers, retry backoff, KV cache hit ratio, SOC2 / data residency questions, staging soak plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run 45 minutes ish, recap of the weekend run and triage the 5xx spike, jamal will jump into traces in a bit
[00:18] Laura: thanks, yeah we saw a couple of customer-facing 502s yesterday during the morning batch jobs, about 1.2% of requests in a 10 minute window spiked, most were short lived but some hit 20s latency then retry cascaded
[00:37] Jamal: ok curious — do you have the exact timestamps and sample payloads? that helps map to KV cache TTL patterns we saw in staging
[00:50] Omar: yes, i'll upload the log bundle after, but quick note — our client retries are aggressive by default, and we added a 1s fixed retry which probably made it worse, we were trying to be conservative
[01:05] Priya: just to flag security — any logs you share should be sanitized, can't include PHI, and give us a sense of retention so compliance can sign off
[01:20] Maya: absolutely, we'll coordinate redaction. jamal, do you have the initial trace overview?
[01:28] Jamal: sure, so looking at the traces we pulled from staging — in the spike windows we see a higher proportion of cold KV misses, followed by longer scheduling times in the inference queue. The runtime then emits 5xx on token generation timeout a few seconds later. There's also a pattern where the token-level latency distribution has a heavy tail up to 18-22s
[01:55] Laura: hmm that matches what we saw, the retries then re-flood the pool, and rate limiting kicks in which gives 429s for some callers, or 502s for internal routing failures
[02:12] Omar: question — do you surface the rate-limit headers on the hosted API? we saw a generic 429 but no Retry-After, hard for our library to back off correctly
[02:25] Maya: currently we surface X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset but not Retry-After consistently. that's a gap we should patch; jamal will follow up
[02:36] Jamal: yeah we can add consistent Retry-After and make the reset window more granular, and include a short human-readable reason code in the header
[02:47] Priya: excellent — for our compliance team it's important to see explicit headers for automated backoff, reduces repeated retries which can cause data exfil risk in misconfigured clients
[03:00] Laura: also are there any differences you expect between hosted and dedicated? our plan B is to move to a dedicated pool if we can't stabilize this
[03:12] Jamal: dedicated will give you fixed capacity and isolation which reduces neighbor noise. but it won't fix aggressive client retry logic or cache warmup behavior; component-level instrumentation is the real fix
[03:26] Maya: agreed. dedicated buys predictability and SLA but we still need to tune cache priming and backpressure controls in the runtime
[03:34] Omar: on cache, is the eviction policy LRU now? we saw a lot of small short-lived conversations which could be thrashing the cache
[03:42] Jamal: it's an LRU-ish hybrid — smaller sequences get higher priority, but under bursty traffic we do see churn. we can expose hit/miss metrics per model and per route
[03:52] Laura: perfect, if we can get those metrics into our prometheus stack that'd help correlate with client logs
[04:01] Omar: about telemetry gaps — when we pulled traces we couldn't join client-side retry timestamps to server ingress consistently. there's no request id propagated in all cases in our SDK
[04:15] Maya: so two workstreams: add consistent request id propagation and enrich headers; and add Retry-After header and more granular rate-limit fields
[04:26] Jamal: for the longer term we should also add a circuit-breaker on the Redwood SDK side to introduce randomized exponential backoff and jitter. we'll provide a recommended config
[04:37] Priya: from security side we also need an explicit doc on log redaction and data residency for the staging runs, and the retention policy for any logs you share
[04:48] Maya: noted — we'll send the redact checklist and sample sanitized bundle template
[04:55] (crosstalk)
[05:00] Laura: can you also share the burst profile you used in staging? we used a bunch of distributed cron jobs that may have aligned, would be helpful to reproduce
[05:10] Jamal: yes we'll dump the JMeter profile and a per-second qps chart. planned soak: 10k requests over 30 minutes with synthetic backoff patterns matched to your client
[05:22] Omar: quick question about 5xx semantics — sometimes our infra returns 502 for upstream transform issues, not strictly runtime errors, can you map error classes?
[05:34] Jamal: we categorize 5xx into timeout, runtime exception, resource exhaustion, and upstream proxy errors. we'll export a sample mapping and the trace-level tags so you can filter
[05:47] Maya: recap of immediate asks — customer to upload sanitized 5xx logs and example payloads; Redwood to run staging soak and add headers + request id propagation; Jamal to instrument cache metrics; Maya to send security/redaction doc
[06:05] Laura: timeline sounds good, aim to have the data to you by Thursday, and we can reconvene after the soak results
[06:15] Omar: one last thing — would it help to temporarily cap client concurrency from our side during the soak to avoid cascading retries?
[06:22] Jamal: yes please, cap concurrency to 5 per client and add randomized backoff, that'll make the traces cleaner
[06:31] Priya: thanks everyone, appreciate the coordination
[06:36] Maya: thanks all, we'll share the playbook and schedule the follow-up for Friday 11/07, same time
[06:44] (call ends)
